:::{#exm-cond-expectation-function}

#### The conditional expectation function of the birthweight model

Continuing @exm-cond-pdf and @exm-cond-expectation,
$(X, Y)$ (gestational age, birthweight) is modeled as bivariate normal.
The general form of the conditional mean derived in @exm-cond-pdf,
evaluated at an arbitrary $x$ instead of just $x=`r x0`$,
gives the conditional expectation function directly:

$$
\ba
g(x) &= \mean_Y + \corpar\frac{\sdpar_Y}{\sdpar_X}(x-\mean_X)
\\&= `r round(intercept, 4)` + `r round(beta, 4)`\, x
\ea
$$

which is exactly the fitted regression line
(the general algebraic identity
$\mean_Y + \corpar\frac{\sdpar_Y}{\sdpar_X}(x-\mean_X) = \paren{\mean_Y - \corpar\frac{\sdpar_Y}{\sdpar_X}\mean_X} + \corpar\frac{\sdpar_Y}{\sdpar_X}x$
is what makes the bivariate-normal conditional mean linear in $x$).
As a check, evaluating at $x = `r x0`$ recovers @exm-cond-expectation's result:

$$g(`r x0`) = `r round(intercept, 4)` + `r round(beta, 4)` \times `r x0` = `r round(intercept + beta*x0, 2)` \text{ g}$$

:::
